subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: HOW MWCC ORDERS A TU'S OWN .sdata2 CONSTANT POOL, and therefore how to repair one at source. FOUR CLAUSES, all measured on pb_window.c. (1) LAYOUT IS STRICTLY CREATION ORDER, WITH PADDING - there is no hole-filling allocator. MWCC walks the literals in creation order and inserts 4-byte alignment padding whenever an 8-byte double follows a 4-byte float at an odd word. Proof that it is not hole-filling: laying pb_window's pre-fix creation order out under a hole-filling rule (promote a later 4-byte entry into each alignment hole) packs to exactly 0x70 with zero padding, but MWCC actually emitted 0x78 with pads at +0x04 and +0x24. So a pool that is too LONG is diagnostic of a wrong ORDER, not of a surplus constant. (2) CREATION ORDER IS SOURCE-TEXTUAL ORDER, functions taken in definition order and literals taken in the order they are parsed within each function. Verified against MWCC's own @NN pool labels, which ascend monotonically with file position: debugScissor's @37-@43 map one-for-one onto its source lines in order (the 0.0f truth test, then 0.5 and 1.0 from `0.5 * (1.0 - (double) zoom)`, then the 0.0 of the `!=` guard, then the 1.0f of `1.0f - s1`, then the 2^52 int-to-float magic). (3) ONLY CODE-GENERATED FUNCTIONS CREATE POOL ENTRIES, AND A DEAD-STRIPPED ONE STILL COUNTS. A plain `static` function that nothing references is still code-generated by MWCC, still creates its literals in its source position, and is then dropped from the image by mwld's dead-strip - so it orders the pool without contributing .text or disturbing the .text order of anything else. This is the repair device: pb_window's leading seven entries (0.0f, 1.0f, 90.0f, 2047.0f, 0.0, 4095.0f, 65536.0f) are produced by a static window-defaults helper placed ahead of every other function, and adding it took the pool from 0x78 and mis-ordered to 0x70 with 19 of 20 entries in exact target order, with every function's text bytes unchanged. claimcheck accepts the resulting .text overshoot explicitly ('dead-strip is normal'). (4) THE NEGATIVE HALF, which is what makes the device precise: an `static inline` function that is never expanded creates NO pool entries. Changing the same helper from `static` to `static inline` dropped .sdata2 straight back to 0x78 and .text back to its original size. So the ordering device must be a real out-of-line function; an uninstantiated inline is inert. COROLLARY FOR DIAGNOSIS: creation order is NOT emission order. In pb_window the target creates 2.0f before 0.5f yet uses 0.5f first in the text, so a pool-order repair cannot be read off the instruction stream - read it off the pool, and expect that naively moving the owning statement to fix the pool will move its code and regress the text (measured: 70 -> 108 differing words).
